title: Understanding Bias-Variance Decomposition
text: The bias-variance decomposition is a way to express the error of a model as the sum of three components: the variance of the model, the bias of the model, and the irreducible error. Think about how each of these components might behave in different types of models.

title: Exploring Non-linear Models
text: Non-linear models can capture complex patterns in data that linear models cannot. Consider how this ability might affect the bias and variance of the model.

title: Bias-Variance Decomposition for Non-linear Models
text: Does the bias-variance decomposition apply to non-linear models when using squared loss?
